Kenzo: I think, I think we leave the statue. And then if it turns out there is a way to turn them back, then, you know, people in town can go—
DM: Doesn't seem likely the statue will be further damaged sitting in this temple.
Seeker: And it is—so it's missing the arm and the severed arm is down inside—
Delwath: I just wonder if we want some way of identifying—
Seeker: Well, I can Minor Illusion it.
Seeker: I just have to very carefully memorize what it looks like, I guess.
Seeker: I'll make a drawing. That's good. I—

interactions.title: The horse is recovered alive
lines: DM: So, as—as discussed last time, you do indeed find the horse alive, if a little bit thirsty and annoyed at you for leaving it trapped in an earthen box for, what, 24 hours roughly. But no real worse for wear. ((Hauling temple goods and returning to the road))

before: DM: Tell me what you want.
Wellby: I think—what we're gonna get from here, right?
Delwath: Yeah, yeah. Stuff and head back to—
Seeker: Make haste.
Unknown: Town.
after: DM: Well, first of all, you're going along the road instead of cutting through the canyonlands, so it's an easier journey. Unknown: Huh.

DM: What struck—well, things that seemed to be, you know, those of you who maybe were less familiar with the area, maybe seemed to be normal, now seem to have been disturbed. And as you're riding back, you do sense the sort of difference that destroying this thing seems to have made.

DM: But it's a relatively uneventful journey back to town. People are starting to gather now for the—for the Festival of Rebirth, and so the road is not completely empty. You do occasionally pass people or see groups of Dunmari with their sheep or their horses coming in from the pastureland, mostly to the north. Many of whom give you a wide berth as you're walking from the—from the Blasted Plains and are a bit of an atypical traveling group for this area.
DM: But unless you want to—sorry, go ahead.

interactions.title: The horn’s horse motif and the decision not to blow it
lines: Kenzo: Blow the horn while we're, like, kind of out far away?
Delwath: What does it look like again?
DM: It's a, it's like a ram's horn. Carved with—like, etched with a fine design of a running horse on it.
Delwath: Where did we find it in the temple?
DM: In the tower. In the tower next to the body of a Dunmari.
Kenzo: I guess we could just go and show it to somebody and see if they can help us identify. That'd be—
Wellby: Like, what if it's a horn of summoning wild beasts for murder?
Unknown: But what if it's, yeah.
Delwath: What if it summons somebody to help us, but you can only use it once?
Kenzo: All right, all right, all right, let's not blow it. Save it.
Kenzo: Alright, well, we'll, we'll see if somebody can help us identify it.

before: Kenzo: We solve all their problems and become the greatest heroes.

Seeker: I'm—Tim, when we stop for meals, or no, maybe at, like, lunchtime. You say—here's the thing. I'm using my Stonecunning, because I know that somebody mentioned that there was, like, weird stuff you could dig up along the road side.

DM: Oh, yeah, that was Alesh, the scout you ran into. Yeah, she was referring to, like, relics of old battles, mostly. So your stone sense detects—it won't detect, like, weapons generally. It's only—it's going to detect, like, minerals or, like, precious metals or gems or something. You could—I guess you could try and find—yeah. Let's see. No, you don't sense anything particularly unusual when you stop.

DM: Well, let me just check one thing. No, it's, it's—you seem to—as you're getting further west, it seems like this area has been more—like, a lot of that—probably a lot of the old artifacts and stuff have been found this far—this close to Karawa. But you don't really get a sense that there's anything particularly unusual within your radius.
DM: Okay, anything else you want to do on the journey? For you.
after: DM: Okay. Okay, so, um, as you—

DM: As you approach the town, you can see that—from, you know, from a distance, from the outskirts—you can see that the feeling of the town has changed dramatically in the week or so since you left. Many people have—clearly, the population of the town swells for the festival, right? And you can see now that there's, you know, dozens of camps set up on the sort of flat, dusty grounds on the outskirts of town, sort of to the west and north of the tavern, of the caravanserai. There are sort of many large fields of horses and sheep and goats milling around. Just a general sort of feeling of—of energy and sort of bustling. A swell of people. There's, there's probably—I mean, that the normal population of the town is maybe only a few hundred people at most, and it's probably at least doubled, if not tripled, since you left. There's a large—so, if you remember, one of the features of the town was this large, open market that mostly stood empty. It's now starting to fill. You can see, as you're sort of coming down, in the distance some brightly colored wagons that Wellby recognizes as probably a traveling group of halfling merchants, perhaps come into town to sell wares for the festival. It just—there's a—there's a sense of energy and just kind of bustlingness about the town that—it was just very much, of course, much quieter and, and much smaller and more of a—not a backwater exactly, but just not a lot happening before.

DM: So it's late afternoon now. You head down the hillside where you, Kenzo, were coming down and first saw the giant hyenas attacking, and find yourself now again on the outskirts of the caravanserai.
Kenzo: Shall we head to the temple? Shall we try to find Candrosa?
Delwath: I want to find Kisa first. She was the one who actually sent us on the get-go, right? The town village elder.

interactions.title: Kisa hears the report and recalls the Summer of Red Storms
lines: DM: You—you are quickly directed to this, this council chamber, where you find Kisa walking in shortly after you arrive, slowly. She's, she's older. She has a bit of a limp and, and moves deliberately, but she seems quite pleased to see you back alive, and turns specifically to Delwath and says, "It's been very quiet the past three days. Do you have good news to report?"
Delwath: We found a source of these disturbances, we believe. About three days ago we destroyed it.
DM: That is indeed very good to hear. I am—with the rumors that have been, you know, coming in with the travelers gathering for the festival, I've been quite nervous for Karawa.
Delwath: Were there any further attacks?

DM: Not here, but several—several families were attacked a few days ago on the road north—the road coming, coming from the north—by a large group of axebeaks. I don't know if you've seen them. They're human-sized—they're large birds, flightless, but bigger than a human, with sharp claws and sharp beaks. And sadly, a few people were killed by a marauding horde of them. They're not—they're not—they're not carnivores. They don't normally attack people or animals, but they seemed to be in a—well, the stories I've heard is they were in a rage, and the only way people could—the only way the survivors escaped was to flee on their horses and leave behind their sheep.
DM: That is all that I've heard, but that was—well, the survivors arrived in town a couple nights ago. I'm not sure exactly when the attack happened, but—before, but—more than two days ago.
Kenzo: Remind me the names of the people that we ran into again on the road.

DM: Alesh was the scout who told you about the ruins along the road and said she was going to head for—head for town after trying to alert people to return as quickly as possible. And then Akan was the older man who you met at the—
Kenzo: With that group of guys that all got—they were, like, down there at their campsite, and said—
Kenzo: Whatever. “Have you seen Alesh and Akan?” I ask her.

DM: I do not know Akan. Alesh has been riding hard to the north and west to warn people of these dangers. She reported that she saw you on the road maybe five or six days ago, I believe. She came into town briefly and then headed back out to try and warn as many people as she could. Akan—if he and his family are—likely may be here. There's now—we've had many families come in and set up. Some familiar, many new every year, like we see. And she seems a little bit—you get the sense she's not, like, a particularly huge fan of the festival, to be honest. Like, the town gets busy and she doesn't know people. She's also pretty much directing—I mean, she'll answer your questions, but she's—tends to be focusing her conversation pretty much on Delwath and Kenzo. She seems a little bit—just a little bit, like, maybe even a little bit shy about people she doesn't know.
DM: She clearly knows Alesh. Do you know what the cause of this was? Is this something that might happen again?
Kenzo: I pull out the staff and just show it to her. We destroyed this.
DM: She, she looks at it and she seems like, she kind of mutters and says, "I, I don't understand this. I am out of my depth here."
Kenzo: Do you know who might be—understand what this is?
DM: Do you know these, these carvings?
Kenzo: I do, I can read it.
DM: What, what is it? What writing is that?
Kenzo: It's Draconic. No, isn't it?
Kenzo: What is it? It's a—it's the—
DM: No, I'll tell you. Yeah.

DM: Draconic is not something you would see commonly, right? It's quite unusual. She definitely seems taken aback and, like, like drops it and, like, takes a few steps back and says, "I am—I'm at—I'm—I don't know what this says. I'm—I do not understand. It's just—"
Wellby: Come on, the village is safe. Village is safe.
Delwath: This—we think this was an artifact from the Great War that somehow got out. It is somebody going—
Kenzo: Is there someone in town, you know, that might be able to help us learn more about this stuff?

DM: I'm just an old woman now. I wouldn't know who to talk to, anyway. This is all beyond my—this is beyond my experience. Sheep and water and, and dates and—that's what I know about. This—this is not, this is—it's been 40 years since anything's come from the, from the east and that was just a very—that was a bad summer, but over quickly, and I hope that's not happening again.

DM: She kind of sighs and looks—looks kind of sad, like remembering a bad memory. “The Summer of Red Storms.” It was two months. The two hottest months of the year, there were several attacks all across the border. These creatures, they were vicious. They were almost like hyenas, but on two legs, and they would run in packs across the land, and if they saw you, if they could catch you, they would attack, and they wouldn't even stop to wait till you're dead before they tried to eat you.
DM: But within a couple months, something changed and they stopped coming, and it's been safe and quiet ever since. I really hope those times are not coming back.
Delwath: Seeker. The sketch of the man.
Seeker: We found near the place where we defeated the creature wielding that strange staff a stone statue of a person who looked like this. You know nothing about this person?

DM: Doesn't look Dunmari. He's definitely not somebody from Karawa. You might ask Ikram, the tavern keeper. He, he would know all—he likes talking to strangers, he would know all these people coming through. But I can say for sure he's not from this—this person is not from Karawa.

Kenzo: Well, I think, to the best of our knowledge and understanding, whatever has been causing these troubles recently is, I think, for now, taken care of. We felt, certainly, a great sense of ease in the land upon destroying the staff. So I think our sense is that the festival and everyone that is here should feel safe and should be able to enjoy this period, hopefully in peace.

DM: She kind of breathes a—just a deep sigh of relief and sits. She says, “Thank you. Thank you, Kenzo.” And looks at you, Delwath, and the dwarf and you. “What were your names again?” Sorry, the dwarf and the halfling.
Delwath: Oh, she knows you. Yeah, I'll introduce the two of them. This is Seeker and Wellby.

DM: Thank you, Seeker and Wellby, as well. I will rest easy tonight. It has been a stressful few weeks, to say the least, and I will keep you in my prayers. And if you talk to them, tell them your, your food and drink is on the town.

before: Seeker: Governor, whatever, as a town, there's—
DM: Just a sort of informal sense that, that she's the one who kind of guides the discussions and can sway people to her side.

DM: Generally speaking, the governance of—in this—at least, the eastern part of Dunmar—is pretty informal. There's not—there's not a lot of—it's not, you know, organized into—it's not like, you know, right, baronies with feudal lords, or anything like that. The people kind of—all the land is held in common, and the people kind of spread out and graze their herds, and then there's the small villages. There's a few larger towns. Kenzo, of course, you spent time outside of Tokra, which is a bigger town along a river where there's more agriculture.

DM: Okay, so it doesn't take you that long. Once, you know, you let it be known around town that you're back—and certainly people recognize you—and just the sight of the four of you coming into town, anyway, creates a bit of a stir, simply because it's sort of unusual to see an elf, a dwarf, a human, and a halfling all traveling together. And, you know, it doesn't, it doesn't take you long to, to hear that—for Kisa to hear that you're back, and you find your way to, sort of through the—

DM: So in the main part of the village, there's the, you know, there's, like, these sort of mud huts that kind of form small roadways through them. But there's one space that's kind of more open—so there's the area around the oasis that's more open. Then there's another space that's more open that has this, like, big public square. On one side, there's a similar pentagonal building to the one you found in the fortress. That's the Temple of the Five Siblings here, smaller and less grandiose than the Shakun mystai, which are carved—which is this large monastery carved into the side of the red cliffs of the mesa just south of town. But then, on the other end of this plaza, there's a circular building that serves as the council chambers and that sort of meeting hall for, you know, when the town gets together to have discussions and, and make decisions and—
after: Delwath: Is there, like, a religious leader other than—

The temple here is really clearly a temple of Jeevali, even though it acknowledges her siblings, and Suma's, like, the priestess of Jeevali who is in charge of the temple. The temple is just across the plaza from here.
Delwath: I just was thinking maybe we should return the religious artifacts.
Kenzo: Meta question on Seeker and Wellby. Where are you from again, Seeker? And Wellby, where—
Wellby: Wellby would have to think about what to say. Hang on, I gotta look them up.

interactions.title: Ikram identifies Arcus and shares news of travelers
lines: DM: And just in general, the atmosphere, again, is pretty—pretty, pretty lively, even though there's still sort of an undercurrent of, like, people talking about these rumors about the attacks and, like, do you know anybody who was attacked, and things like that. But Ikram sees you all coming in together and sort of yells across the room. “Kenzo! Look, everybody, it's the one who killed the hyena. Do that thing with your staff. You were supposed to come talk to me and tell me some stories.”
Kenzo: Oh, I've got stories. To drink, yeah. What do you have to drink, my friend? Yeah, we're—we're, we're thirsty.
Kenzo: Nice. Mead, mead, mead. Well, where are you from again, my Seeker? From where?
Seeker: I'm Seeker of Highkeep. That's—

DM: I know that. He was—he was staying here before the two of them got up and left in a hurry. Waiting for some more stories of—what was it you like to talk about, Seeker? Some sort of weird geometry?
Seeker: You know they have a lot in common, those two areas. More stories of rocks. Just rocks. Yeah.

DM: He laughs. Now, so the, like, typical summer afternoon drink that they serve as, like, a slightly sweet, chilled, slightly effervescent, sort of like honey wine made from fermented dates. There's also, like, a vodka style drink fermented from milk, and then they have—
DM: Iced tea, mint, and a few other kinds as well. Whatever your pleasure, on the house.
Kenzo: What are you guys having?
Seeker: I'll have a mint tea.
Kenzo: Ikram, what are you drinking?
DM: I'm drinking whatever you're drinking Kenzo.
Kenzo: You're drinking— I asked you first.
DM: Okay, I'll bring a surprise.

DM: He heads back in, and he goes, gathers up a few things, and comes back soon with three tall glasses—tall mugs—of, like, chilled mint tea, a few, like, snack things, like flatbreads with goat kebabs, and two mugs of a spiced beer, sets them down in front, and says, “Okay, story time.” As you're—
Kenzo: Well, we had a question for you first. I think Seeker—Seeker has a drawing that he'd like to show you, curious about—

Seeker: There's a lot to tell. We've explored and seen many things, but we found this one weird thing, which is a stone statue of a guy who looked really surprised. Maybe his arm had recently been bitten off. We don't know, but it looked like this.

DM: He looks—he looks a little bit puzzled for a moment. Yes. You say that's a statue? Looks just like this man named Arcus who passed through here, I don't know, four or five weeks ago. Didn't stay longer?

DM: One night. He was kind of quiet. Didn't say much. Not from this town, not from around here. I tried to get him to chat, you know. Don't see that many strangers coming through, although, to be fair, there's been a few more strangers than usual lately, actually. A little bit unusual to have coming through in the winter, but now that I think about it, I can't say Arcus was the first. He kept to himself. He didn't—he didn't— he didn't chat much. He seemed like he was going somewhere. Yeah, in his traveling clothes, just did the one night.
Wellby: Could you tell where he was from? His accent, or did he say?

DM: I don't think he was Dunmari. I don't know where he came from. He—you know, that reminds me, he paid with this—his silver was odd. It wasn't normal coin. It was these small coins that had a portrait of a man on one side, and a, like a staff with light shining off of it on the other. It's not something I'd seen before.
Kenzo: I recognize—so that's from—didn't we find old Chardonian coins in there?
Wellby: Remember, we were looking at Tenser's Disc itself, like the coin that forms the Tenser's Disc was a Chardonian coin, an antique Chardonian coin.
Kenzo: Definitely sounds like a Chardonian—Chardonian silver coin.
DM: From Chardon. That's a ways away. Wonder what he was doing in these parts. Why—anyway, he wouldn't tell me.
Delwath: Did he talk to anybody else while he was here?
DM: Ah, that's a good question. He, you know, he might have talked to the smith, Jasu.
DM: He was asking. He was asking about, about, you know, who knew about metals.
DM: Seemed interested in artifacts for some reason.

DM: I don't know. I thought maybe he had—he had picked up something on the road, you know. People often find, you know, spearheads or, or, or bits of horn or sometimes even shields or weapons along the road. You know, there was a, you know, in the Great War, there was a bunch of battle sites around here.

DM: Not so close to Karawa. Actually, you may not know this, but the Temple of Shakun here actually dates from before the Great War. But certainly along the trade road, there was—certainly some battles there. People, you know—people say there was a few great battles here that, you know, some of the great heroes of that age might have even ridden through here, and I don't know, maybe he found some—maybe he found something on the road.
Kenzo: You know who in town might have a sense of knowledge around artifacts, who might be able to identify artifacts or tell us more about some, some artifacts?
DM: Well, you know, you know, actually, the person who is the most interested in—in the history of the Great War around here—I don't think she's around right now, though—is Alesh. Alesh, sorry.
Seeker: That's who we ran into. Yeah.

DM: Yeah, that's even on the road, um, every time she stopped, she keeps asking about, "Oh, has anybody found anything new? Are there any more things I can try and collect for my amateur museum? Ikram, what have you heard about battle sites?"

DM: That's who I'd ask if I wanted to know about some Dunmari artifact, but I think she headed north before you is—well, let me just stop and say, I assume the fact that you're all back here in one piece, and nobody's dead, means that whatever was attacking our town is gone.

DM: Alesh had—had gone to warn people and, you know, and try and get people to town. Sadly, she didn't warn everybody. I don't know if you heard, but there's been—a few people have come back recently after reporting attacks. Ikram sort of gets kind of sober and quiet for a minute.

DM: You know, there was—there was Akan, whose family, I believe, is now camped out on the outskirts of town for the festival. And he said he—oh, maybe it must have been you he was talking about. He said he met some travelers on the road who had killed some beasts. But his family was attacked by giant lizards. And there's another traveler—there's another Dunmari pastoralist family who's come in, Devana, who—his family was attacked by axebeaks, these large birds that have sharp claws and, and, and sharp beaks that normally don't even attack people or animals. They're not even really predators.
DM: You know, we were just talking about a family, so let's have a moment of silence for the dead.
Seeker: He pauses for a sec.
DM: But in town for the festival—
DM: Competitions that happened in the—in the—after the festival with the big fair and, and celebration and—

DM: Well, the archery and horseback competitions tend to be more artful displays of skill. I have to say, the axebeak-riding competition is one of my favorites because I have never seen so many people fall comically off an animal before. So if you're in town, try it out.
Wellby: You mentioned, too, that other—you've seen more travelers than usual coming through, especially in the winter. Were there others like this last guy?
Wellby: I mean ones who struck you as unusual, not just—

DM: Yeah, that maybe—you know, we get some odd types coming to try every now and then the, the Temple of Shakun, and that's a bit of a sight to see, I must say, and the red mesa is unusual in these parts. So you never quite know who's coming through. And every now and then some, you know, wild thrill-seeker will head out to the east to see what they can find. Most of those never come back, I have to say.
DM: Yeah, I'd say maybe a few might have been like him, sort of quiet and kept to themselves and didn't stay long.
Kenzo: Anybody else with these Chardonian coins?
DM: I can't remember. I'm sorry.

before: DM: Inn first, okay. Ah. So the inn is—let's see, what do we got here? The inn is not quiet and peaceful. The inn is bustling and—
Unknown: This is not going to be the right music.
Kenzo: Works.
DM: Too Western. We'll go with this. It's not perfect.

DM: Okay, so yeah, so the inn is—it's definitely—when you were here a week ago, there was, you know, probably almost nobody else. A few other people staying there, but not really very many people. Now it seems like almost every room is full. There's a handful of people sort of lounging outside, sitting around with drinks in the afternoon, kind of chatting to each other. There's—the courtyard is, is sort of on the outside, is full of animals. Here we can go back to the map. Back in town.
after: Kenzo: Yeah, we understand but I know you're in search of stories. I will share one part of our adventure.
Seeker: As a part of—

Kenzo: I think what helped to keep the village safe—we had to battle what seemed to be some kind of strange hobgoblin sorcerer of some kind. I've never seen anything quite like it, and I wonder if you've heard of anybody like that, or heard of anything about hobgoblin spellcasters.
DM: Hobgoblin sorcerer? He, like, makes a five-pointed star. “Five Siblings keep us safe.” Ah, I don't really want to hear about more hobgoblin sorcerers. Keep them in the Blasted Plains.
Delwath: Rather hear about how a—Seeker built a barn with no door for my horse.

interactions.title: Ikram’s cockatrice story and offer of lodging
lines: Seeker: I wonder if you know anything about chickens that can turn each other to stone.
DM: Again, I have never heard of a chicken that can turn something—
DM: Cockatrices? Is that what you're talking about?
Seeker: We think that's what those were, yes.
DM: They, they live out in the desert. They're rare. They're kind of pests sometimes, but the nice thing is that if they turn you to stone, it doesn't seem to last.
DM: If they turn you to stone, you know, a minute later, you're back to normal. I heard of—

DM: I heard a story from, from one of my friends. She told me that one of her sheep got turned to stone once. Yeah, and this little cockatrice and the sheep just kept pecking at each other, and the sheep would turn to stone, and then the cockatrice—seems odd that they turn things to stone, because what do they eat? Fair. Never thought about that.
DM: Anyway, she ran off and she left the sheep because she—
Seeker: Did not want to be turn to stone. But—

DM: Actually, as she was riding away on her horse, the sheep turned back. Then the cockatrice pecked it again, and it turned back to stone. And I think eventually she was gone. And then I don't know what happened.
DM: But yeah, but they are not common. But they're around. I've seen them.
DM: I know people who have seen them in the desert. They—they make—they dig underground. They lay their eggs in—in caves and underground pits, supposedly. That's what I've heard, anyway.
Seeker: I wonder if we should go find that Smith.
Delwath: So you've never heard of a cockatrice turning somebody to stone forever?
DM: I've only heard of this one sheep. I don't know what happened.
Delwath: And have you by any chance heard of any magic that might turn you back?
Seeker: Candrosa's the one to ask about magic.
DM: Sure, I'm, I'm—the best I can do is pour a nice tea or a mug of beer.

DM: Candrosa's probably at the temple. Yeah. It's getting towards dinnertime. Why don't you—why don't you stay and talk and go find these people in the morning? Can't be that urgent. I don't know, maybe it is.
Kenzo: You know, I think maybe we'll go and try to learn a little bit more. And we'll come back after for dinner. How's that sound to you all?
Seeker: We'll have to eat late. Yeah.
DM: Okay. I'll save you a table.
DM: And rooms, because I've only got a few left, but I can save them for you if you need them.

before: DM: I'd like to see that someday. Maybe you can arrange a demonstration.
Seeker: Perhaps we'll get our chance.
DM: Fascinating. You've got some of that magic mumbo jumbo, don't you?
Delwath: Can't build barns, though.
DM: True, true.
after: Unknown: See you later.
DM: Delwath has his own—Delwath has his own room. He has a house across the—room above a tea house across the street.
Seeker: Nice.
Delwath: And stabling for the horse.
DM: The horse will probably be stabled here.

interactions.title: Wellby and Seeker compare their mapping projects
lines: Wellby: Is, like, the major landmarks and stuff copied over from other maps. And then it's, like, a detail as it goes.
Seeker: Right, so, so, Wellby, you've got more maps like this?
Wellby: I mean, I have my own notes from up north, but I really only started this project once I came over these mountains and headed south. That was when I got serious. Is—this is—
Wellby: You know, the maps—the maps have, like, a lot of detail around Dunmar.

Seeker: I've been, you know, sketching my observations of ley lines, but it's more of a piecemeal approach. I would love to integrate and synthesize these findings all together. Your, your larger scale maps could help with that.

before: Kenzo: Trying to—
Unknown: Oh.
Seeker: What's that unlabeled city in the middle of the plains, on the west side there?
DM: That's just another city on the—that's, like, the border of Dunmar. That's just something. Wellby just had heard of that. There's—this is not—this road continues, but you just don't know.
DM: This is just—Wellby is not entirely sure exactly. You know where Chardon is just because everybody knows where Chardon is. This town you've heard of on the border of Dunmar. You just got this—
after: Kenzo: Do these ley lines move, Seeker?
Seeker: Well, my impression is that's a bit like asking if mountains move. Yes, yes, of course they do.
Kenzo: But slowly over time.
Seeker: That's my impression. And occasionally, all of a sudden, catastrophically, like at this point on the map. And I point to the giant rupture in the belt of mountains to the north.
Kenzo: What happened there?

interactions.title: Jasu discusses Arcus and the resistant spearpoints
lines: DM: You get to Jasu's blacksmith shop pretty much as he's finishing up in the—I don't know what I did with my town images as well—as he's finishing up in the—he's, like, just sort of dousing his forge and getting ready to head in for dinner, and he sees Delwath. He sees you coming and he sort of turns and—"Delwath, can I—can I help you? Do you need something?"
Delwath: Apologies for catching you at the end of the day, but we had a few questions about a man you might have talked to several weeks ago.

DM: Okay. Ah, what if you give me a moment? He's, like, an older man, sort of bulky, solidly built. "I'm, I'm just putting away all my stuff now. And I was about to head to Ikram's, just to have a drink in the coolness of the evening. If you'd like to come that way and join me, I'd be happy to chat."

DM: So he takes a few minutes to kind of store his gear and just clean up the, the smithing area and says, “Okay, let's head along.” And you can tell he's probably here a lot. Ikram sees you coming, anyways. He sits back, and Jasu sort of heads to the regular table and sits down. Ikram brings you all more drinks of the same thing you were drinking before. “Okay, so what would you like to talk about?” This is Jasu.
Delwath: I'll gesture to Seeker. There was a man here a few—
Delwath: Arcus. Arcus. Arcus, the man here a few weeks ago.
DM: Elf. Would you introduce me to your friends?
Delwath: Oh, yes, of course. I'll introduce the three of them.
Seeker: So I take out the drawing to show him.

DM: That looks familiar. It was a man who is here several weeks back. Went by the name of Arcus, I believe. He talked to me because he had found something. I don't know where, actually. He seemed quite interested in ancient Dunmari artifacts from the Great War. A little strange, actually. I don't know why. I think he was from—definitely not Dunmari. He was from out west somewhere, Chardon or somewhere in that direction. I don't, I don't know why he would have taken an interest in our history—artifacts, but he seemed to—that's what he seemed to care about.

DM: And he had a couple of spearheads that he had found, silvered, um, and wanted me to haft them for him. He seemed to indicate he was expecting to be traveling back through town in the next couple of weeks, but he never came back. Where did you—where did you say you got that picture?
Seeker: Well, I, I drew the picture of him. What—
DM: Where did you meet him?
Delwath: He's, um—he encountered an accident.
Seeker: To be honest, we're not quite sure what happened. We found a stone statue of him, to be precise.
Kenzo: Seems a cockatrice got him.

DM: I'm—to be honest, I can't say I'm too upset. He was—seemed a bit pushy. Like, you know, this land is this—I got the sense he wanted to come dig up our history and bring it back somewhere with him, and I don't know about that. Seemed rather, um, sure of themselves.
Seeker: You mentioned he asked you to do something to those spearpoints. What exactly was it again?
DM: Ah. Oh, he wanted me to haft—just attach them to wood, to make them into weapons, right? They're just the spearpoints.
Delwath: The spear points—he found them on the road?
DM: Well, he didn't say exactly. I kind of assumed that, I guess.
Delwath: And would you be willing to show them to us?

DM: Yeah, I'd be happy to. In fact, it's a bit odd, they seem—well, it's silver, or even silvered metal shouldn't be that hard to work. But it—I don't know, I haven't been able to haft them. They seem to be—I don't know what to say about them, exactly, other than they seem to be resistant to my attempts at smithing them. Like, almost they don't want to be damaged. They're in quite good condition. They seem rather new.
Seeker: I'm an artisan myself, but mainly of stone and glass, so I'm interested to hear about your experience.

DM: Well, so he sort of goes into a long description of, like, nothing, and, like, talking about all the technical details of exactly how you put spears on—on wood and the best practices and things like that. It's, like, the punch line of it all is that he couldn't. He just seemed like he couldn't drive—he couldn't drive anything—he couldn't melt the metal or reforge it in any way, or drive anything into it. Seemed like it was way harder and more resistant to heat than it should be.
Seeker: Tim. Tim, did we find things like that in the temple? Did we find some spearpoints?
DM: Just—just some amulets—amulets. It was—so all your—
DM: Right, that's—it was—it wasn't—although you ended up using it as a weapon, it wasn't technically a spear. It was, right, a holy symbol of Aagir.
Seeker: Right. Well, we'd love to see those spear points.
DM: Come by my shop in the morning. I'll, I'll dig them up for you.
Kenzo: And Jasu, do you know much about other artifacts?
DM: You know, the person you should talk to if you really want to know about Dunmari artifacts is Alesh. But I think Ikram told me she's out. She was riding to tell people about the beasts.
Kenzo: If she were to return, do you know where we might be able to find her?
DM: Ah, I'm sure she'll stop in at Ikram's. She'll come here to just say hello to people. She does have a—she lives in the village, but she's not hard to track down.
Seeker: And have you ever made a harness or saddle for an axebeak?
DM: You think of entering the competition?
Wellby: No, I'm thinking of winning.
DM: The thing about axebeaks—I'm not really a saddler. I tend to work strictly in metal, not leather.
DM: The thing you got to remember about axebeaks: their backs are not flat. They slope like this. So if you let go for even a second, guess where you're going to end up? On your butt.
Seeker: It's spoken like words from experience.
DM: Oh, I have never entered the competition. That's for younger than me. It's quite fun to watch, though.
DM: Although, I must say, it gives me—it gives some amusement, but the skill and talent displayed in the horseback riding events are more my taste.

before: Wellby: So, blacksmith.
Kenzo: Sweet.
Seeker: It's sweet. Let's check out the blacksmith, Jasu.
Unknown: Okay.

DM: Ah, he is—as you—so there's the sort of street where Delwath has rooms and the—that the caravanserai is on. There's, like, a series of shops along that street, mostly, like, various craftspeople who live above their shops. So the smith is there, and there's, like, a—what do you call the—tailor—tailor—and, like, hosiery, and a cobbler, and all—that's, like, pretty much the, like, where all the, you know, those people live and—
after: Kenzo: I turn to the rest of the party. There anything else we should talk to you about?
Seeker: There is that one thing that we could show that we have. That's kind of weird.
Wellby: Which thing?
Unknown: The—
Kenzo: Let's find another place to show him.

interactions.title: Bree’s welcome ends when Wellby offers to help her sick companion
lines: DM: Um, so she steps forward, and she, you know, kind of seems a bit—a bit tired, like clearly has traveled, but seems, like, always happy to talk to people. And she introduces herself. She says, "Welcome. I'm guessing, fellow travelers? Most of you look like you're not from around here." You could say. "Name's Bree. Bree Charmheart. Would you like to sit and chat?"
Wellby: We would introduce each of them in turn, and then myself, and say it's good, good to sit with the family.
DM: You too. It's been a long road from Sembara.
DM: Indeed. Are the Goodbarrels—oh. Good. You tend to trade? Is your family—they tend, they tend to circle around the sort of safer parts of Sembara these days.
Wellby: Yes, and good on them.
DM: That sounds like a bit of a boring life to me.
Wellby: That's why I'm here. Not there.

DM: There's more fun and more money to be made, bringing the riches of the Green Sea far afield. We've got some apple brandy, some spices, some furs—let's see, many furs—good wine from Sembara. I'm guessing you're probably not here to shop.
Wellby: You know, interested in trade of different kinds—of information.
DM: Happy to chat. You have—
Wellby: All right, if they're coming down from Sembara, then we probably have less useful stuff about, like, Chardonians. Where'd you go on to from here?
DM: Head west—Chardon. Spend the summer and probably a good part of the winter—the good part of the—the fall.
Delwath: Wait, wait. On the coast? Where'd you come from through Sembara? How'd you get here?

DM: Well, there is a route you can take. Stick close to the mountains along the eastern side of the mountains. There's a few—there's a path that comes across the southern part of the mountain range, follow the river down to Tokra, and then head east to Karawa. We're just here for the festival, to be honest. After that we'll probably head back towards Tokra rather than down the river, maybe pass back across the mountains along the coast, hop a ship up to Chardon, see what we can get there for some of the Dunmari stuff we collect, hopefully with full purses and empty wagons.
DM: Trade the full purses for full wagons, then head back across to the east, and then back to Sembara. The whole route's maybe about a year.
Delwath: Nice to meet other travelers. Any other travelers up—up the mountains?

DM: I'm—honestly, usually not a lot of travel. You'll see the, the occasional wanderer passing through. But to be honest, we tend to give travelers pretty wide berth in those parts. Not always so safe to meet a stranger so far from civilization.
Wellby: Have you seen the festival before?
DM: Oh, yes, I've been. This is my second trip on this circuit. It's interesting.
Wellby: Any tips for riding axebeaks?
DM: Ah, thrill seeker. You probably have an advantage because of your size. Hold on tight. Ah, and don't be scared.
Kenzo: When is this race happening? I'm excited for it.

DM: Um, so just after the—just after the—there's a—there's the Festival of Rebirth, which is worth seeing. And after the festival, there's a fair for a few days. And during the fair, there's games, market, competition. That's when we do most of our business. Ah—
DM: And then she sounds—you know, our—she looks around at you all, and she says, “Is there some other thing you wanted to know or something you wanted to—”

DM: She seems to get a little bit less—almost like you don't know what happened. Like, maybe you said something wrong. She's a bit, a little bit less friendly, says, "If there's anything else." She just, like, looks at all of you pointedly.
Wellby: Don't say anything else for the moment, but I pointedly look off at the wagon in the distance.
DM: Um, now Bree is kind of looking at you, like, impatiently. Like, why are you here? I'm—
Wellby: I'll turn back to her and say—choose my words carefully here. Is it, like, a faux pas to speak Halfling in front of non-halflings?

Wellby: I'll say to her, "You're traveling with someone sick," and then I'll emphasize that with, like, the Halfling word for sick, with a connotation of someone sick in spirit, not just in body, which presumably there's some Halfling word that gets the nuance of that just right. "You're traveling with someone sick. Let us help you. I think the sickness that they have is a sickness that we saw just two or three days ago."
DM: Persuasion check with advantage because—she says, "Why do you say this? I'm not sure that you should linger much longer here." And to the rest of you, she seems to have gotten very cold.

Wellby: Three days ago, in the caves northeast of here, beneath an abandoned stronghold, we found a staff that spoke to us in the same voice that seems to speak to your sick companion—when I use, again, that Halfling word for sick. We managed to destroy the voice there and then. But it sounds like this one still hears it. It makes me suspicious that it's spreading.
DM: So as, as you're saying this, you, you hear—you hear a noise and a disturbance coming from, like, the, the wagon that's a little bit in the back. And—

DM: Bree turns around, and you see, sort of stumbling out from the wagon, a disheveled-looking halfling. He's dressed in sort of raggedy clothes, like totally unkempt hair, like wild. It seems like not even slightly, you know, taking care of himself or bothering to, to, you know, pay attention to the, you know, personal hygiene or anything. And he's, like, sort of looking around wildly, and he sees Bree, and he says—
DM: “He spoke to me.” And he points at Wellby, and he says, “He spoke to me.”

DM: And then he sort of smiles, and this, like, look of peace comes over his face, and he says, “The master will eat me soon.” And then he sort of—and Bree, like, turns around and looks at you and says, “Really, now, I think you must go,” and rushes back over towards him and says—and, like, tries to calm him down and, like, “Rest, rest,” like walking back towards the wagon.
Wellby: I raised my hand in this sort of conciliatory gesture and say, "We'll talk again."

before: Kenzo: You got quite a few skills there.
Wellby: It's more like the lute musical talent skips a generation, maybe.
Kenzo: By the way, this is random, but none of you have ever seen, like, a monk drink beer before, just in general. So, no.
Wellby: Are monks, like, a thing in general, like, or—

DM: Yeah, they're a thing. I mean, like, many of the mystai—you know, the Dunmari mystery cults are basically monks, right? There's certainly, in the Dunmari religion—there's—that's what—you know, that's what the sort of monkish monastic tradition would be, is all these, like, mystery cults.
after: Kenzo: Are we carrying the staff with us? We are, right?
DM: Yeah.
Kenzo: Just, like, I mean, I know we've destroyed the thing that's, like—what if it still kind of, you know, activating or—oh, no.
Delwath: We really think it's the same thing?

Wellby: Well, so I assume we'll sort of—yeah, slowly head on. So it's a strange thing. In the wagon, this halfling—I spoke with him. He said that someone's been talking to him. He says, "The master is waiting. You'll find joy with the master, the master wants you to come and join us." Over and over and over. Asked him to name the master, and he said, "The master is my master. Master will consume the world and bring us joy." I asked him how he heard the master's voice. He said, "It talks to me all the time. It's endless. It never stops." Maybe it's not the same thing. But I feel like that staff. I mean, when the hobgoblin held it up—

interactions.title: Wellby recounts the sick halfling’s unceasing voice
lines: Wellby: Well, so I assume we'll sort of—yeah, slowly head on. So it's a strange thing. In the wagon, this halfling—I spoke with him. He said that someone's been talking to him. He says, "The master is waiting. You'll find joy with the master, the master wants you to come and join us." Over and over and over. Asked him to name the master, and he said, "The master is my master. Master will consume the world and bring us joy." I asked him how he heard the master's voice. He said, "It talks to me all the time. It's endless. It never stops." Maybe it's not the same thing. But I feel like that staff. I mean, when the hobgoblin held it up—
Wellby: It spoke in a certain way. Maybe it's—
Kenzo: No, I think you're onto something.
Seeker: This is no good. Did you have a sense of how long this guy has been in this state?
DM: I mean, just from looking at him, the brief glimpse you saw—seemed like, you know, like he looked pale. He looks sort of unkempt. Definitely more than a few days.
Delwath: But possibly something he picked up on the way through the eastern part of Dunmar that apparently nobody should go to.
Wellby: Though they came the same route that I took to get here, more or less.
DM: Right. True. Yes, more or less. More or less. Yes.
Wellby: Or, that is to say, like, the route they took basically came straight south to Karawa. Like, they didn't skirt the mountains to be, like, far off to the east.
Wellby: All right, well that's bizarre.
DM: I think you might have gone further west and come down the road to Tokra and east to Karawa, while they might have come more directly. But yeah, you would have gone through roughly the same.

before: Wellby: I raised my hand in this sort of conciliatory gesture and say, "We'll talk again."
Kenzo: Are we carrying the staff with us? We are, right?
DM: Yeah.
Kenzo: Just, like, I mean, I know we've destroyed the thing that's, like—what if it still kind of, you know, activating or—oh, no.
Delwath: We really think it's the same thing?
after: Delwath: Is it night yet?
DM: Yeah. It's dinnertime.
Kenzo: Like we were saying, maybe we go talk to Candrosa and call it a night.
Seeker: Well—
Delwath: Maybe we should talk to Candrosa in the morning.

interactions.title: The rumored once-in-a-lifetime vision from Shakun
lines: DM: It, it requires—the story is that in order to see a true thing about the future, you need to remain in meditation for the entire night without being distracted or falling asleep. So many—but few, actually, it seems like you—
DM: There are some people who say they who claim to have done it. There's always some doubt as to whether they were really able to remain focused in meditation. Wow. Wow.
Delwath: Also, Tim, sorry to distract you with two questions at once. Is there any rumors about what happens if you go back a second time to the oasis?
DM: Ah, the saying is that you get one vision.

DM: And that's that. But nobody really knows. There are people who have claimed to have gotten two visions, but most people kind of, you know, joke—tease them and say, "You're just making it up at this time. You've never succeeded." The sort of more, like, mystical rumor is that this is, like, a once in a lifetime thing, like—
DM: Shakun will give you one vision of your future, one true thing about your future, and that's the thing you get to know.

before: Delwath: Keep the rooms.
Kenzo: Yeah, I don't think it matters.
DM: There's enough people at the inn, he's probably not tracking your coming and going.
Kenzo: Is it, like—it does the oasis have, you know, on a, like a, like—would it, would it be odd to just kind of sleep there?
DM: Yeah, it's a bit odd. I mean, you know, there is this rumor around town. So every now and then somebody will, like, go try and get a vision or something like that.
after: Seeker: Is this the moment?

Kenzo: Like, this is not a moment, at least for Kenzo. Meditate for eight hours? I feel like this—that's something I like doing, is trying to meditate for eight hours, but actually think I want to get some sleep at night.
Wellby: And I don't want to blow my vision of the future, just to find out that I lose the chicken race.
Seeker: Good to have some mystery in life. That's true. That's—
Kenzo: Delwath, I think I'm gonna—I think I will. I'm excited about, actually, this inner journey, this long meditation that—like, not, not tonight for me.

interactions.title: Candrosa interrupts the oasis vigil
lines: DM: I'm—fairly late at night, maybe 1030, 11pm, as, as you start to struggling to kind of keep yourself from drifting off to sleep, Wellby, you see somebody walking across the oasis from the temple towards you.
DM: Not across the water, no, sorry—across the plaza, right, coming out of the temple. Seems to be heading straight for you.
Wellby: Oh, start going towards them. Okay.
DM: You can tell that it's Candrosa. And he kind of looks around at you and then at your two companions. “What are you doing out here so late at night?”
Wellby: “They're resting. I'm keeping people from bothering them,” I said with a broad smile.

DM: He kind of gives you a flat look. He says, “I think there's much we must discuss. I heard news you had returned. I was expecting your visit. Think we better speak now. I've had some—had a message.”
DM: He's, like, looking around again. He says, "Where's Kenzo? Where's the fourth one of your party?"
Wellby: I think he was going for a drink last time I saw him. I say as vaguely as possible.
Wellby: Yeah. Do you want us to meet you there? Should we meet you at the temple? What's, what's good for you?

DM: Again, looks at you kind of like—he's not smiling. He's like, you know, stop joking around. And he says, “Yes, please fetch him,” and then he, like, walks over to Seeker, kind of shakes him awake, and says, “Dwarf, we must speak.”
Seeker: I get to my feet. "You must be Candrosa." We've heard a lot about you. It's good to meet you.
DM: No, you met him. He was at the—in the first session. He spoke with you briefly when you were, um—
Seeker: I thought we didn't meet him.
DM: Right after the hyena attack. Him and Kisa both came.
Wellby: Yeah, I'm not gonna take orders from him.
DM: You're not? Okay, he's looking at you.
Wellby: Well, I'm gonna wait and check in with, with my companions. I don't care what mystai human is going to boss me around. So I make eye contact with the two of you. "Shall I go get Kenzo?"
Seeker: Seems like a habit. Yeah, the best.
Wellby: Very good. Head off to get Kenzo.

lines: DM: Ikram also—he has been, like, you know, drinking with you and telling stories. Yeah, he's also a bit, um, you know,
Kenzo: I like to shout at them, like he's, like, sitting at a table.
DM: He's, like, also two sheets to the wind, and he turns around and he shouts, like, at the empty chair next to him, like he's about to shout, and then is like, "There's no one there."
DM: And he gets up and he, like, staggers over and he says—
Kenzo: The halfling's got three eggs and a stick.
DM: He, like, brings three raw eggs in their shells to you and grabs a ten-foot quarterstaff from next to you. And have—
DM: Hands that to Wellby and says, “This is a pretty big stick for a halfling.” That's gonna do.
DM: Hands you the three eggs.

DM: Ah, just roll a d20, but roll twice and take the lowest roll.

lines: DM: A man walks out of the temple, like, after Candrosa was headed back, and, like, rides past you on a horse. He seems like—you haven't seen really too many people who seem like skilled warriors, like well armored and well equipped. But this guy definitely seems like that. Like, he's young. He's, like, boss. He's got a spear and armor and, like, just gallops across the—the common. He comes out of the temple and then gallops across the plaza and heads—heads out of town for—or heads out away from the oasis, like towards the inn. Away from the oasis. And you see this. You see this guy also, like, barrel past you, Wellby and Kenzo, as you're coming out of the inn, heading basically to, like, the area where people are camping.

before: Wellby: All right.
Kenzo: I'll be back. I'll be back.
Wellby: We're going to go talk to a mystai.
Unknown: So—
DM: Seeker and Delwath, as you are waiting, like riding—like—
after: Seeker: Um—

Kenzo: All right, so I'm just kind of, like—I've got my staff, leaning heavily on it, and just sort of, like, stumbling with Wellby, trying to get myself, like, together a little bit here.

But he, he sort of leads you to a little bit of a side room where there are some chairs and a table that you can sit at, and he, when he sees you all there and he sees that he, you know, clearly interrupted tonight, he does, you know, seem slightly apologetic and, you know, looks at you all and says, "I'm sorry. I didn't mean to disrupt your night like that."

DM: I was just needing the news from your travels. I've heard, of course, from Kisa and from others that you were—you are able to destroy the thing that seemed to have been causing the troubles we had. But since then, I've received several pieces of news that suggest that this may not be as simple as we thought.
Kenzo: Kenzo just takes the staff out—like, the iron staff—and just, like, throws it on the table. He's like, that's what we destroyed.
DM: Sort of looks at that and he says, “What is this?”
Kenzo: We thought you would know more than us.
Delwath: An artifact of the Great War, we think.
Wellby: There was a gem on top of it, which we destroyed.

DM: Um, he—he, he looks at it and he says, “I have studied a bit of bit of our history. It does seem perhaps from the Great War. What, what—why did you say it? Why do you think it was from the Great War?”
Wellby: Can I guess? This feels like a weird reaction.
DM: This doesn't look to me—
Delwath: You misunderstand me. Which side of the Great War did you think I was referring to?
Delwath: No. That sort of artifact.
Kenzo: Do you recognize these runes, these writings, Candrosa?
Delwath: The—the creature—the reanimated dead that was wielding this was clearly a follower of my—
DM: He looks a bit taken aback. Up—I thought that was ancient history.
Wellby: I'll speak telepathically to each of the three of you, in turn, just very quickly. He's hiding something.
Kenzo: Where are you hiding? Takes, like—what are you hiding?

DM: He, he actually almost looks not relieved, but not surprised that you said that. And he sort of sighs a little bit, and he says, almost to himself, sort of looking off into space, “The four of you... Such an unusual group to see these days: a dwarf, an elf, a halfling, and a human meeting when you did and coming here for different reasons but arriving just exactly in time. It seems like it cannot be a coincidence. Some sort of hand of fate is at work here, but whether to aid us or for some other purpose, I cannot see. And whether to trust you...” It's not clear. It seems like he's talking to himself. Or do you just say that, “Who is us?”
DM: I want to trust you. I wish I could trust you, but I don't know if I should. What brought you all here again? How did you meet?
Wellby: We met on the battlefield. I mean, when that attack came, each of us ran toward—
DM: At least you ran toward it. But why were you here? Why did such an unusual group of people end up in our little village?

Seeker: Personally, I'm on a quest for understanding. I heard about the mysteries that you explore here from 1000 miles away, and made my way here because maybe you could help me find some answers, to make some, some connections between the worlds that I've explored.

DM: He looks, like, sort of—let's say, he looks at you and he seems to be sort of almost trying to peer, like, into your mind. Any—and he sighs. He, like, almost breathes a bit easier. And he says, “At least the dwarf seems honest.”
DM: You must understand from my point of view. While I am grateful for your aid, all of you are strangers to this town. You ask what I'm hiding. I must know if there's anything you are hiding first.

Wellby: I'll say, “You know, I didn't come here for any dramatic reason or seeking adventure. I spent my whole life in and around Sembara, and all I wanted to do was find the empty places on the map. There's not a lot of empty places in Sembara. There are a whole lot down this way.”
DM: There are indeed empty places on our border. Well, perhaps not empty, but empty on a map. And he, he looks at you all, and he says, “Are you willing to trust me for a moment?”

Kenzo: Kenzo looks at Candrosa and is like, “I didn't want to meet you under these circumstances. I apologize.” Burps loudly. What—but I had been looking for you, Candrosa, for a little bit of time. I was sent here by Speaker Lora, and you're actually the reason why I'm here. So hopefully we can talk more later, but not my best moment right now. I apologize.

Delwath: Looks just like a little bit, almost like he's not meditating, exactly, but, like, he's not—he's kind of staring off into space. He's not exactly paying attention to the conversation. He looks like he's kind of maybe deep in thought. After a minute, he kind of looks up at him and says, "I've been looking for answers for what happened to me for some time now, and I had hoped that the—the mysteries of Shakun would help find these answers. So it's been quite elusive. You have been quite elusive in the town, and do not share your wisdom willingly or easily."
DM: He kind of sighs and says, “I ask again, please, will you trust me?”
DM: Yes. Okay. You see, him starting to cast.

DM: Okay. He says, “Please don't be alarmed,” and he starts—takes out, like, an amulet that he clutches in his hand, and he starts muttering a chant in a language that you don't—that you don't understand, under his breath, just quietly, like almost like nonsense words, and this energy starts to move out from him. And you feel, as it passes through you, this, like, wave of—of magic, like sweeping around a 15 foot circle that surrounds all of you, but, but not him.

DM: He's casting Zone of Truth. ((Spell area, resistance, and duration)) While you're inside the Zone of Truth, you cannot respond to any questions with a lie. You can choose not to answer them, but you cannot tell a lie.

DM: And he relaxes a moment as this spell kind of washes over everybody, and he says, “Before I say anything more, I need to know: do you have the interests of Karawa in your heart? Will you aid us, or will you hinder us?”
Kenzo: What have we been doing here this whole time?

Delwath: That all those who are—Delwath will say, "Since I joined the battle against Cha'mutte 300 years ago, I've always been—I've always aided those who oppose the forces of evil. If that is you, then yes, I will aid."
DM: Seems to relax as you all—as you all sort of answer, and he knows the spell that, that nobody is hiding anything. And he says then—

DM: Like, his, his whole demeanor changes and he seems almost like he was just carrying this, like, nervousness and tension, and he then asks you, “How much do you know about the Great War?” I guess some of you know quite a bit.
DM: Ah, but you may not know so much of the aftermath here.

DM: While the great evil was defeated, Dunmar itself was in chaos. Many, many had died, including most of our strongest warriors, our leaders, our heroes. And although the great enemy was dead, the mystical plague of his creation was still spreading and the land was rocked by upheavals and destruction. It was a very desperate time for the Dunmari, and we lost much. Only over the—only over the next few generations were we able to slowly recover, claw our way back from the brink of destruction.

DM: And during this time, Shakun blessed us with her power. And through her aid, we were able to create defenses along our borders. Great magic of hiding and protection, such that those evil creatures that would do us harm found themselves lost in the desert, unable to find a way forward, unable to make their way past into Karawa, into the heart of Dunmar.

DM: But now, for reasons I do not understand, Shakun seems to have abandoned us. These attacks that started three and a half, four weeks ago signal to me that something must be wrong. Even these beasts—they seem to have unnatural rage in their hearts, and the evil they brought was not deterred by these protections.

DM: I have just heard news of even worse danger. Rampaging creatures, half human, half hyena, have been fought just south of here. And Havdar has just come from a battle on this side of the border. Again, this could not have happened if she was still watching over us.

DM: I do not know what has changed. I do not know why these dangers spill over our borders now. There are some mysteries of the Shakun oracle that are even kept from me. But if Shakun has really abandoned us and these ancient defenses have really fallen, I am frankly terrified for the future of Dunmar.

DM: Well, I do not know what to do about it yet. I would, from the bottom of my heart, beg you to come to our aid at this moment. If Shakun cannot protect us, we will have to rely on more mundane forces.

DM: And he sort of pauses, and he closes eyes briefly, and he says, “I wish I could talk to you under better circumstances. You especially, Kenzo. I—I wish I could help you understand what you're seeking. Seeker, too—I know many of you have come here with questions. Delwath, about your past, but right now—”
DM: Shakun is gone, and I don't know what to do.
Wellby: A halfling tonight among the caravan, who was crazed, who heard voices speaking unceasingly in his head.
Seeker: And I'll relate back the stuff that he was saying.
Wellby: It seems connected, though I can't say how.
DM: He then—he then he sort of—I—closes eyes again. “One more for the list. I had not heard that rumor. You may not have heard, but—”

DM: I've also received reports of a lightning storm that will not end to the northeast. And of course the rampaging humanoid hyenas to the south. It seems in all directions our borders are beset. This cannot be happening.

DM: And he looks, like, like really honestly terrified. He says—he, like, almost offers up a prayer, and is like, “Shakun, if it's something we did, if it's something I did, just give me a sign. Why have you left us?”
DM: And then it sort of goes quiet. Sign.

Wellby: Well, I turn back to the three of them and say, "To be honest, I would love to go to any of those places. Never ending lightning storm? That sounds amazing. Hyena people—I've never heard of this. And granted, this is all a horrible tragedy. I'm in for it."
Delwath: Yes, but how can we help? Is going and looking at unending lightning gonna solve anything?

Kenzo: Well, I'm sorry, guys, I'm just a little bit annoyed right now that we were put in some kind of a circle of truth to test whether or not we were going to do something positive for this town. And we spent the last eight days trekking through desert, trying to kill some, like, staff—like, staff thing and mind-controlled hobgoblin, fighting off these hyenas, trying to save as many villagers as we possibly can. And this is the main question that's being asked of us, is whether or not we care about the people here. It's a little frustrating. Sorry to say—I got the answer, Candrosa. Again, I'm sorry, but—

DM: He looks—he looks, like, a bit embarrassed, and he says, “I understand, Kenzo. Just—if the town knew, if the people knew, especially just before the festival, there would be panic. That would be disaster.”
DM: They've been counting on us to protect them for generations.
Wellby: What's going to happen at the festival if she doesn't—

DM: Well, the Festival of Rebirth is not Shakun. It's Jeevali. It's one of, like, part of the main—he says, "Perhaps—it's late. Perhaps it would make sense to discuss in the morning with—" Sorry, I forget his name. I just said is—actually making the morning—
DM: It would make sense to discuss with Havdar in the morning, find out more of what he knows before we make any decisions about what might be helpful to do. I—

DM: And he kind of, like, looks at you all again. He says, “It is, I must say, a relief to confide in somebody, and I don't know what to do to keep the town safe, to keep Dunmar safe. But at least through the festival, knowing that you are here and you are watching would give me great relief.”
DM: It seems there are many mysteries on our borders. News—news of this halfling makes me nervous.
DM: And there will be time in the week before the festival to discuss these more. But now it is late and perhaps rest would be the right decision. Yeah.
Kenzo: I agree with that sentiment, Candrosa. I personally apologize for not meeting you under better circumstances, but I think I'll have better wits about myself in the morning.
DM: He, he says, “Before you go, I am—I am sorry for the circumstances.”

DM: And he sort of reaches around and he grabs from, like, a—out of a pouch tied around his waist, like, four small, fist-sized vials that seem to contain, like, mud that—but that doesn't dry out, that just kind of stays mud, and he says—
DM: Please, as a token of my good faith and as a token of thanks, take these. They will heal you, should you need it. Each of you.

DM: I am—I am sorry for how the past few months have been, but you must understand this is generations that the town has looked to us as their guardians and has trusted Shakun. Something has changed recently, something—I don't know what, but this can't be—this can't be coincidence. This can't just happen for no reason.
DM: And we will talk more in the morning. Please.

DM: And he sort of, like, bows slightly, almost apologetically, and a little bit—again, a little bit relieved, and, um, still a bit—you know, you can, you can tell he's not, like—you know, he wishes, he again, he wishes circumstances could have been different. And he was just quite nervous about the town. And the whole border.
